$schema_note: Shared cross-validation fixture for the path-confinement engine. Both the TypeScript engine (mcp/typescript/src/path/confinement.ts) and the Python engine (mcp/python/src/artifacta_mcp/path_confinement.py) must produce the SAME accept/reject verdict for every case in `cases`. AF_MCP-6.2 cross-validation test consumes this file from both sides.

$semantics.verdict_allow: Engine returns ok=true (TS) / ConfinementAllow (Python) for an absolute, existing, regular file inside the allow-list and not on the deny-list, within the size ceiling.
$semantics.verdict_deny_outside_allow: Path resolves outside every allow-list root.
$semantics.verdict_deny_denylist_root: Path resolves under a built-in deny-list root (e.g., ~/.ssh, /etc).
$semantics.verdict_deny_denylist_pattern: Path matches a deny-list filename pattern (.env*, credentials.json).
$semantics.verdict_deny_special_file: Path resolves to a socket, FIFO, char device, or block device.
$semantics.verdict_deny_size_exceeded: Regular file exceeds the size ceiling (caller-provided or 500 MB default).
$semantics.verdict_deny_unresolvable: Path cannot be realpath()'d (ENOENT or symlink loop).

$placeholders.$CWD$: Replaced at test time with the absolute path returned by os.getcwd() (Python) / process.cwd() (TS).
$placeholders.$HOME$: Replaced at test time with the absolute path returned by Path.home() (Python) / os.homedir() (TS).
$placeholders.$TMP_REGULAR_FILE$: A regular file inside CWD created by the test harness — fixtures referencing it assume the harness wrote >=1 byte and the file exists.
$placeholders.$TMP_DIR$: A temp directory inside CWD created by the test harness.

cases.note: Default case — a regular file inside CWD is allowed.
An absolute path outside CWD with only CWD in the allow-list.
/etc is always denied even if / is allow-listed. Cross-validation: TS resolves /etc/hosts to itself or /private/etc/hosts on macOS; both engines must match either way.
The classic tripwire — even with $HOME allow-listed, ~/.ssh is denied.
.netrc is a single file rather than a directory but still listed as a deny root.
Filename pattern fires regardless of allow-list. Harness creates $TMP_DIR$/.env.
ENOENT before deny-list / allow-list can fire.
